summary: The College Transparency Act requires the National Center for Education Statistics to establish a secure postsecondary student-level data system. This system will track student enrollment, progression, completion, costs, financial aid, and post-college outcomes while replacing the prior federal statutory prohibition on a student data system. Colleges that participate in federal student aid programs are required to submit the necessary data, and the Department of Education must provide adequate staffing and report to congressional committees quarterly on implementation progress.

affected_groups.effect: Will have access to customizable, complete information about college costs, financial aid, and post-college outcomes to help make education decisions, and can request inspection and correction of their personal data.
Participating colleges must collect and submit student-level data to the Commissioner, while the system aims to streamline reporting requirements and reduce overall burdens.

Agencies such as the IRS, Department of Defense, Department of Veterans Affairs, and Social Security Administration will participate in periodic secure data sharing, and states will receive aggregate feedback reports and query capabilities.

key_provisions: Requires the Commissioner of the National Center for Education Statistics to develop and maintain a secure postsecondary student-level data system within five years.
Repeals the existing statutory prohibition on creating a student data system under the Higher Education Act of 1965.
Establishes a Postsecondary Student Data System Advisory Committee to help determine data elements and ensure privacy and security.

Mandates periodic, privacy-protected data matches with other federal agencies, such as the Internal Revenue Service and the Social Security Administration, to evaluate student earnings and employment outcomes.
Requires the creation of a user-friendly public website and analytic tool displaying summary aggregate information on student access, progression, completion, costs, and outcomes.

Prohibits the inclusion of sensitive individual information such as health records, student discipline records, elementary and secondary data, exact addresses, citizenship status, political affiliation, or religion.
Directs the Department of Education and the Commissioner to provide dedicated staffing and submit quarterly progress reports to specified congressional committees.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or appropriations dedicated to establishing and maintaining the data system and staffing.
Exact technical specifications of the database architecture beyond references to NIST standards and federal guidelines.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The College Transparency Act requires the National Center for Education Statistics to establish a secure postsecondary student-level data system. This system will track student enrollment, progression, completion, costs, financial aid, and post-college outcomes while replacing the prior federal statutory prohibition on a student data system. Colleges that participate in federal student aid programs are required to submit the necessary data, and the Department of Education must provide adequate staffing and report to congressional committees quarterly on implementation progress.
summary_detail.significance: The bill impacts all postsecondary institutions participating in federal financial aid and all students attending them by creating a comprehensive federal student data tracking system. It alters federal higher education policy by removing the long-standing ban on student-level databases, establishing strict privacy and security parameters, and mandating transparent public reporting on college outcomes.
